title: Dairy-Free Banana Spice Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft banana spice cupcakes with a dairy-free crumb, ready in about 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake time.
description: These cupcakes start with ripe mashed banana and warm spices like cinnamon and nutmeg. I tested this batch in my home kitchen three times to get the crumb soft, not dense.
ingredients: 1/2 cup neutral oil (canola or melted coconut oil)
1 cup mashed ripe banana (about 3 medium bananas)
1/3 cup unsweetened dairy-free milk (oat or almond)
1/2 cup dairy-free vegan butter, softened, for frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, baking soda, salt, cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger in a medium bowl.
In a large bowl, beat oil, granulated sugar, and brown sugar until smooth.
Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition.
Stir in mashed banana, dairy-free milk, and vanilla extract until combined.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mix. Stop as soon as no flour streaks show.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each about two-thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat dairy-free butter and powdered sugar until fluffy, then pipe onto cooled cupcakes.
tips: Use bananas with brown speckled skins. They mash smoother and taste sweeter.
Do not overmix the batter once flour goes in. Overmixing makes a tough crumb.
Room temperature eggs blend faster and help the batter stay smooth.
Let cupcakes cool completely before frosting so the topping does not slide off.

faq.question: Can I use frozen bananas for this recipe?
faq.answer: Yes, thaw frozen bananas fully and drain any extra liquid before mashing. Too much liquid can make the crumb dense.

faq.question: What dairy-free milk works best here?
faq.answer: Oat milk gives the softest crumb because of its natural creaminess. Almond milk also works but the texture is slightly lighter.

faq.question: Can I skip the frosting and still serve these?
faq.answer: Yes, these cupcakes taste good plain since the banana keeps them moist. A light dust of cinnamon sugar on top works well too.

faq.question: Why did my cupcakes turn out dense?
faq.answer: This usually means too much banana or overmixed batter. Stick to 1 cup mashed banana and mix just until the flour disappears.

conclusion: These banana spice cupcakes are simple enough for a weeknight bake and soft enough for a special occasion. Store leftovers in an airtight container for up to three days.
